$comment: Maps external auditors' issue taxonomies onto the butler's fixed 35-item checklist.
act           - a real defect; fix it through the normal plan -> approve -> apply flow
edge          - real, but the repo is not at fault; the fix is in the CDN/host dashboard
verify        - the auditor is often right AND often wrong here; prove it before acting
informational - not a defect (a capability notice, or a state that is usually intentional)
`subjectIsUrl` means the finding is ABOUT the URL rather than about something on it, so a dead
page and the links pointing at it collapse into one job instead of two.
`falsePositive` records a MEASURED disagreement, not a suspicion. Each one was reproduced
against a real site before being written down. Do not add entries here from intuition -
an unverified suppression is how a real defect gets silently dismissed forever.

blocked-page.note: The crawler was challenged by bot protection. Often a WAF/Bot Fight Mode setting, not a site defect - cdn-layer.md.

canonicalized-page.note: A page pointing its canonical elsewhere is usually deliberate.

noindex-page.note: Auth, error and thank-you pages SHOULD be noindex. Only a fail if the page is meant to rank.

heading-order-skip.note: Invisible on screen - level and size are styled separately. Verify with validate-artifacts.mjs, not by eye.

thin-content.note: Body content. Propose in the plan, never rewrite silently (safety.md).

deep-page.note: Click depth. Real for content pages, expected for paginated archives.

tech-https.note: Mixed content is explicitly part of item 11.

tech-broken-links.falsePositive: Warns 'requires site-wide crawl mode' when run on a single URL. That is a statement about coverage, not a defect - there is nothing to close. Get the real answer from validate-artifacts.mjs --url, or re-run geodaddy with --max-pages.

cont-json-ld.falsePositive: Reports 'missing required @type' on JSON-LD that uses the root `@graph` pattern - {"@context":…,"@graph":[{Organization},{WebSite}]} - because it only looks for @type on the root object. That pattern is canonical schema.org and correct. VERIFIED 2026-08-02 on a real site. Before acting, parse the blocks yourself: validate-artifacts.mjs reports the real @type inventory.

geo-listicle.falsePositive: Flags every page without a numbered list or table, including ordinary prose. checklist.md item 18 is explicit: check listicle structure only where the page really is a list, and never force it onto prose. Acting on this blindly damages real content.

geo-schema-stacking.falsePositive: Wants Article + ItemList + FAQPage on every page. checklist.md item 9 and standards.md forbid adding a type the visible content does not back. Stack only what the content genuinely earns.

$lighthouseComment: Lighthouse is already the butler's performance layer (measurement.md), run locally through the
chrome-devtools MCP so there is no quota and no API key. What was NOT being used is its SEO,
accessibility and best-practices categories, which are an independent auditor in their own right
- Google's own, and the one users mean when they say 'my Lighthouse SEO score'. Those findings
are adjudicated here alongside the crawlers instead of being read and forgotten.
Keys are Lighthouse audit ids, stable across versions.

crawlable-anchors.note: Links a crawler cannot follow (JS onclick, no href). Also a GEO Tier 1 problem - geo.md.

is-crawlable.falsePositive: Fails on any page carrying noindex, which is CORRECT for auth, error and thank-you pages. Lighthouse cannot know intent. Only a defect when the page is meant to rank - checklist item 11.

structured-data.note: A manual audit: Lighthouse never scores it. Use validate-artifacts.mjs for the real JSON-LD verdict.

urlPatterns.note: Cloudflare injected this URL; it is not in the repo. /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection is Email Obfuscation (Scrape Shield) rewriting a mailto: - the crawler gets a 404 and never sees the address. Fixed with a dashboard toggle, never by editing the link. VERIFIED 2026-08-02. See cdn-layer.md.
